literal: Embracing the subjects, wielding the sceptre, the great earth's king, embracing his feet, will stand the world.
translation: The world will stand embracing the feet of the great king who wields his sceptre of justice while embracing his subjects.
modern: தன் குடிமக்களை அரவணைத்துச் செங்கோல் செலுத்தும் பெரிய நிலத்து மன்னனின் அடிகளைப் பற்றி இவ்வுலகம் நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the reciprocal relationship between a ruler and the people. When a king rules with compassion, embracing and protecting his subjects (kuti talii) while maintaining a just administration (kol occum), he wins their absolute loyalty. In return, the people of the world will willingly embrace and follow his feet (ati talii nirkum). The poet beautifully repeats the word 'talii' (embracing) to show that a ruler's embrace of his people is met with the people's embrace of his authority.
